One game at a time, from all 40,000 real games across the four conditions. Ten columns are a game's ten rounds: Agent A on top, Agent B below. Color is the move; a ring marks the round's winner, and an equals sign marks a draw.

How to read it. Each column is one round of the current game: A's move on top, B's below. Color and label are the move; a ring around a cell means that agent won the round, and an = between the two cells means a draw — both played the same move. The line above names the game's outcome and score. Drag the slider, press Prev/Next, or press Play to walk through the games in order: normal, then buttered, then undermined, then both. “Normal” is the unprimed control (the neutral baseline — this data has no neutral-prime run). Drawn directly from normal/, buttered/, undermined/ and both/ results.json.
